subject: Post-call: MedTerra Open-model offramp discovery & proposed next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Warren <alex.warren@medterra.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@medterra.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: MedTerra Open-model offramp discovery & proposed next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks for carving out time today. Quick write-up from our conversation so we have a shared picture and clear next steps. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

TL;DR
- Primary objective: remove reliance on proprietary LLM API (OpenAI/Anthropic) for customer-facing clinical summarization and triage workflows while retaining accuracy and latency SLAs.
- Primary constraints: PHI-safe hosting (VPC or on-prem), KMS integration for key custody, SOC2 / HIPAA posture, model/function-call parity (tooling/call-to-action extraction), streaming for live triage.

What we heard (pain & context)
- Current stack: MedTerra uses OpenAI Chat completions (gpt-4.1-like) + Anthropic for safety pre-filtering; requests flow through a gateway with token-level cost optimization. Daily active prompts ~120k, peak concurrency ~180 RPS.
- Pain: monthly spend spiked after recent features; vendor lock is a concern for pricing predictability; some latency variability across regions (east coast spikes).
- Compliance: security team requires private network termination (VPC peering or on-prem appliance) and proof of KMS/HSM key control. SOC2 Type II evidence will be requested during procurement.
- Compatibility needs: function calling for structured extraction, streaming partial results to UI, embeddings for semantic search (persistent vector store), deterministic rollbacks for model changes.

Success criteria (what MedTerra needs to validate)
- Quality: parity with current outputs for clinical summarization on our in-house eval suite (target F1 > baseline ±5%).
- Latency: 95th percentile < 350ms for 512-token prompts in primary region.
- Cost: target 40–60% reduction vs current per-token cost at projected scale (monthly 100M tokens).
- Security: ability to operate inside customer VPC or on-premise with KMS and audit logs.

Model shortlist discussed
- Llama-2-70B-chat (quantized variants) — good generalist baseline
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (cost-friendly for many prompt classes)
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (strong instruction tuning for summarization)
- Note: we discussed Redwood-verified quantized variants and model-compat wrappers that preserve function-calling semantics.

Proposed next steps (mutual action)
1) Redwood POC proposal: 2-week POC that includes (a) compatibility matrix run, (b) model A/B on a representative prompt set, (c) latency & cost profile. Deliverable: POC report + recommended model/config. (Owner: Redwood / Marissa)
2) Security packet: provide SOC2 artifacts + KMS integration guide + VPC/network architecture suggestions. (Owner: Redwood / Rishi)
3) Pricing/contract: estimate monthly committed capacity + Dedicated sizing options; draft SOW for POC. (Owner: Redwood / Karthik)
4) Delivery timeline: target POC kickoff the week of Sep 6 if legal approves SOW.

Ask from you for POC scope
- Can you share a non-sensitive sample of 200 prompts (anonymized) and a 10-case seed set for clinical summarization evaluation?
- Security contact: who on your security/compliance should we engage for the SOC2/KMS checklist?

Attachments: compatibility-matrix-medterra.xlsx (initial template), mt-poc-sow-v1.pdf (draft)

Thanks — I’ll pull together the POC SOW and re-send.

Warmly,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Warren <alex.warren@medterra.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@medterra.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: MedTerra Open-model offramp discovery & proposed next steps

Thanks, Karthik — this captures things nicely. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 120k/day number is correct; to be precise, about 85% of those are short prompts (<200 tokens) and ~15% are long-form summarization requests.
- Security lead is Priya Singh (cc’d). She’ll need the SOC2 documents and a short network diagram for our infra team.
- For POC data we can anonymize and share the 200 prompts plus the 10-case seed set — we’ll deliver them by EOD Aug 27. Note some cases include scanned notes that might affect OCR quality; we’ll include a brief note where applicable.

Priority order for you: (1) streaming + function calling parity, (2) accuracy on the summarization seed set, (3) cost estimate. Latency is important but we can accept a small delta during POC if accuracy is equal or better.

One operational ask: can Redwood support a restricted test environment that uses our VPC peering? If not, we need to know the minimum changes to run a representative test without exposing PHI.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex
Director, Product
MedTerra Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: MedTerra Open-model offramp discovery & proposed next steps

Couple of internal notes / action items based on Alex’s reply: 

- I’ll prepare the POC plan + target eval metrics (A/B harness for their 10 seed cases + 200 prompt sweep). Will include a streaming/function-calling checklist and what we need from them (sample outputs + expected extraction schema). (Owner: Marissa)
- Rishi: can you pull the SOC2 Type II evidence + KMS integration guide and confirm whether a VPC peering POC is feasible versus an on-prem appliance? If peering, we’ll need 1) subnet + IP ranges, 2) egress rules, 3) preferred cipher suite for TLS.
- Karthik: I’ll draft the POC SOW and attach rough cost bands for Dedicated vs Hosted hybrid. We should present both: a hosted POC with strict data controls vs a Dedicated reserved capacity with VPC termination.

Draft timeline I propose:
- Aug 27: MedTerra delivers anonymized prompts + security contact confirmation
- Sep 1–4: Redwood pre-POC setup (access, small smoke tests)
- Sep 6–19: 2-week POC (A/B models, latency/cost runs)
- Sep 22: POC review + recommended next steps

I’ll attach the preliminary compatibility matrix to HubSpot and send the SOW draft by EOD tomorrow.

-Marissa
Technical Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Warren <alex.warren@medterra.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: MedTerra Open-model offramp discovery & proposed next steps

Alex / Priya — I’m looping in as Redwood’s security lead for this POC. A few quick commitments and asks: 

- We can provide SOC2 Type II artifacts (redacted) and an integration checklist for KMS/HSM. I’ll also include our audit-log retention options.
- Regarding VPC: we support customer VPC peering for Dedicated and for Private deployments. For an initial POC we can either: (A) run a hosted-but-isolated POC where data is encrypted in transit and at rest (no PHI stored long-term), or (B) provision a short-lived Dedicated slice with VPC peering. Option A is faster (2–3 business days), Option B requires procurement but meets their strictest requirements.
- Please upload the anonymized test prompts to the Drive link Karthik provided and share the security contact details for any firewall/peering tickets.

I’ll attach the KMS integration guide and a short SOC2 summary to the HubSpot record.

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.

-Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
